CandidateEvidenceOut.description:
The candidate's evidence references with, for the caller, the views already issued.
``required_index`` is the evidence a decision must have had rendered.
CandidateEvidenceOut.title: CandidateEvidenceOut

CitationOut.description: Derived by backend code from a published evidence row; never model-produced.
CitationOut.title: CitationOut

DatasetKind.description: Fixture and real data are isolated (working agreement 12).
DatasetKind.title: DatasetKind

EvidenceRef.description:
Where a field was read.  A table cell (page, grid, row, col) or a clause line (page,
line, clause path); the excerpt is the exact text of that cell or line.
EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

IngestRequest.description: Register a PDF already present in the source bucket (operator uploaded it there).
IngestRequest.title: IngestRequest

LocalisationDecision.description:
A reviewer's checkpoint decision.  ``confirm`` keeps the detected regions; ``correct``
replaces them with ``regions`` (every region then carries origin=reviewer).  Both need a
rationale and a statement that the pages were looked at.
LocalisationDecision.title: LocalisationDecision

PublishPreview.description:
The consequences of a publication over a scope (Section 7.1, principle 5).  The
token must be presented with the publish request.
PublishPreview.title: PublishPreview

ReviewDecisionRequest.description:
A reviewer's decision on one candidate (Section 7.2).  ``expected_version`` is the
candidate version the reviewer looked at; ``evidence_view_ids`` are the views the image
endpoint issued to this reviewer for this candidate.  A correction is a partial record
(only the listed fields change), a cause tag and an evidence selection.
ReviewDecisionRequest.title: ReviewDecisionRequest

SourceState.description: Pipeline state machine of Section 6.2.  Milestone 1 uses uploaded -> inventoried.
SourceState.title: SourceState

info.description: Data service: sources, inventory, jobs, registry.  Candidates and facts arrive in later milestones as separate resources.
info.title: Tariff Order Intelligence API

post.description:
One of the four outcomes (Section 7.2).  Refused without the rendered evidence, with a
stale version, without a rationale (except approve), without a cause tag and evidence
selection for a correction, or by the first reviewer at second review.  An
``Idempotency-Key`` replays the original result for the same request.

get.description: Correction history, undone decisions included: nothing is deleted.
The candidate's evidence references and the views already issued to the caller.

Render the cited page to the reviewer and record the view.  The response header
``X-Evidence-View-Id`` is what a decision cites; it is issued only here, only to the
reviewer who receives the bytes.

200.description: rendered page with the cited table outlined

get.description: Citation drill-down: the cited page rendered from the immutable source bytes.

200.description: the cited page, cited table outlined

get.description:
Current releases across sources; fixture releases are counted separately and never
presented as coverage.

Screen 6a: wheeling, losses by role, CSS with its derivation (computed / cap /
approved), additional surcharge with decision status, banking, green tariff and
transmission references, each with citations and review state; families with no
published fact are `coverage_insufficient` with the reviewed disposition if one exists.

Screen 5: category tree with components, units, value states, applicability,
conditions and citations, under a completeness banner.  Only published facts.

post.description:
Batch approval (Section 6.10): only high-confidence, no-risk, finding-free candidates
routed to batch, each still with its own rendered evidence and version.  Items are
decided one by one; a refused item never blocks the others and says why.

get.description:
Sources with pending candidates, with the individual / batch split (Section 6.10).
Fixture sources are listed with their flag and never mixed into real counts.

Section 7.6: review time by risk tag, correction rate by cause and utility, outcomes.
No document text, ever.

post.description:
Register a PDF.  Identical bytes are deduplicated by SHA-256; an ``Idempotency-Key``
replays the original response for the same request and rejects a different one.

get.description:
List objects in the source bucket and whether each one is registered.

This is how the three tariff orders reach the system in the cloud: an operator copies
them into the bucket, then registers each one with POST /sources/ingest.

Condition records: verbatim general provisions, footnotes and clause conditions with
the category codes they name.  All `verbatim_only` until a reviewer interprets them.

schema.title: Response List Dispositions Sources  Source Id  Dispositions Get

put.description:
A reviewer records that a charge family is not decided by this order (Section 6.9,
network-charge completeness).  Audited; the next validation run reads it.

get.description:
Provider telemetry per run: provider, model, prompt and schema versions, tokens, cost;
fixture and real runs are counted separately and never summed together.
Authorized access to the immutable bytes.  No signed or public URL exists.
The document-wide heading inventory: the expectation localisation reconciles against.

post.description:
The mandatory human checkpoint of Section 6.5.  Reviewer or administrator only; the
rules never confirm their own result.  A decision queues the structure stage.

The publication transaction.  Fails on a stale source version or preview token, on
missing required items for a `complete` declaration, on undeclared gaps for a `partial`
one, and on approved candidates that still carry blocking findings.

Show what a release over this scope would publish and what stands in its way.  The
returned token is required by the publish call: the consequences shown must still hold.

get.description:
Pending candidates of one order in review order: risk first, then coverage impact,
then confidence (Section 7.2).  Every item says why it sits where it does.

post.description:
Re-run one reading stage (after a rules-version bump, or to reprocess a failed one).
Artefacts from earlier tool versions are kept; new ones are written beside them.

get.description:
Every numeric cell of the confirmed approved regions with its header path, row path,
unit binding and flags (Section 6.6).  ``unresolved_only`` lists what a reviewer must look
at: cells with no header path, no row path or no unit.

Table grids from both readers with their agreement class — the routing signal of
Section 6.4.  The full cell grid is in the artefact at ``object_key``.
